title: ToF-SIMS Imaging and Analysis of Light Isotopes in Irradiated Materials
content: The compositional and microstructural changes in structural and functional materials are critical for nuclear materials in fusion and fission applications. Post-irradiation examination (PIE) of key components of the tritium breeding device that are used in light water reactors can reveal insights of fundamental processes such as isotopic exchange reactions, tritium transfer and retention, and lithium volatilization and transport in the irradiated environment. Such information is also useful in developing breeder blankets for fusion energy. Two components of interest in the tritium-producing burnable absorber rod are the iron aluminide-coated austenitic stainless-steel cladding and Zircaloy-4 cruciform. It is important yet challenging to characterize the light isotope distribution in the neutron irradiated components. We investigated tritium (3H) and lithium isotope (6Li, 7Li) transport within a neutron-irradiated lithium aluminate breeding pellet, cladding, and cruciform at relevant locations using multimodal mass spectral imaging in time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) during PIE characterization.
